origins.section: The Compiler Chooses an Overload From the Arguments' Declared Types
Widening First, Then Boxing, Then Varargs: the First Phase That Fits Wins
null Goes to the Most Specific Overload, and Two Unrelated Ones Don't Compile
Overloads Must Differ in Erased Parameter Types: the Return Type and Type Arguments Don't Count

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-shipper-quote: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-shipper-quote: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-shipper-quote: Page: "At each call the compiler searches the methods of the receiver's declared type, compares the declared types of the arguments, and records which overload to call." Shipper's only quote takes an Object; "equals(Sku) doesn't override Object.equals(Object): its parameter list differs, so it is an overload"; "The object's class at run time takes part in only one choice: which override of the chosen method runs on the receiver".
recorded.prompt:q-charge-cents: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-charge-cents: independent readers: a page-free reader (wording only) and a page reader with the page and the quiz, each a fresh agent
recorded.outcome:q-charge-cents: "The first allows only subtyping and widening (int to long, long to double, char to int), the second adds boxing and unboxing"; "It stops at the first phase that finds a candidate".
